title: On the complexity of two-stage stochastic linear optimization with small second stage
summary: Two-stage stochastic linear optimization is known to be #P-hard when all involved random variables are independently and uniformly distributed over intervals, even with fixed recourse. We show that this problem is in fact #P-hard in the strong sense. More surprisingly, #P-hardness persists even when the random vector is one-dimensional, i.e., uniformly distributed over a single interval.
